dedupe_keys.name: bdwaste bangladesh digestible and indigestible waste images

description: BDWaste contains smartphone photographs for classifying common waste materials in Dhaka-area settings. Uttara University publishes twenty-one class archives on Mendeley Data, covering indoor and outdoor examples of food residues, paper, plastics, glass, packaging and other discarded items. Version 1 is freely accessible under CC BY 4.0. Geographic coverage is local collection sites around Dhaka; calendar acquisition dates are not established. The metadata contain conflicting counts: the description says 2,625 images, the method says 2,624, and the article says 2,497 across twenty classes, not twenty-one. These unresolved count and class differences are material limitations for selecting train-test splits or comparing accuracy. Modellers could test perception components within waste-sorting simulations, with data-waste-concern-bangladesh-waste-database providing separate waste-system context. Images are not measurements of waste mass or composition prevalence. No archive was downloaded, no images were counted, and reported neural-network accuracies were not reproduced.
